items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: Graham Bell was starting to, uh, get a few jobs and play around... Graham organized his band after the war... I suppose next, uh, to Graham Bell's band would, uh, come the Southern Jazz Group

ctx.x: Well, you found other friends who were interested in that.

Yes. There was, um, just at that time, uh, Graham Bell was starting to, uh, get a few jobs and play around, uh, at a few dances. And, uh, this would be the early forties. Um, he, his brother Roger, Ade Monsborough, and, uh, a clarinet player called Pixie Roberts, were the, the first, uh, first line, I'd say, of, uh, Australian jazz. It was in Melbourne, Australia, that it all, uh, seemed to get going. Um, Graham organized his band after the war, and, uh, they did a trip to Czechoslovakia to a world youth…
How did they sound, uh, the, uh, Southern Jazz Group and Graham Bell? Are they... would you think that they had any particular model, or...?
